newsitem.title: UK: B.A.T shares gain on fresh demerger talk.
newsitem.headline: B.A.T shares gain on fresh demerger talk.

text.p: Shares in B.A.T Industries Plc rose in pre-market trade on Wednesday as a press report revived speculation of a demerger of the company's tobacco and insurance arms.
The stock, which last Friday dropped to its lowest level since early May, was up 3p at 549 by 0726 GMT in thin volume of 3,900 shares.

A report in the Guardian said B.A.T would shortly announce plans for a full demerger. It cited documents circulating in London's financial industry that suggest B.A.T had decided its financial arm was strong enough to exist as a standalone unit.

The paper said the demerger was on the agenda following a settlement of U.S. litigation against the tobacco industry -- which could allow investors to more fully quantify the risks the industry is facing.

The report added that B.A.T planned a restructuring to group its retail insurance and investment activities under the Allied Dunbar name, with a direct marketing unit trading under the Eagle Star brand.
No-one at B.A.T was immediately available for comment.
Talk of a demerger of its tobacco and insurance operations has circulated for months, if not years. The company last year had abortive talks to merge its insurance arm with Commercial Union Plc.
CU shares were up two pence at 663-1/2.

B.A.T said at its annual shareholders' meeting earlier this year that a corporate restructuring would be considered if and when it was believed it would improve the company's prospects and boost shareholder value.
